questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the structural features of alcohols and ethers:
Statement I: The $\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{H}$ bond angle in methanol ($108.9^\circ$) is slightly less than the tetrahedral angle ($109^\circ 28'$) due to repulsion between the unshared electron pairs on oxygen.
Statement II: The $\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{C}$ bond angle in methoxymethane ($111.7^\circ$) is slightly greater than the tetrahedral angle due to the repulsive interaction between the two bulky alkyl groups.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. In methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$), oxygen has an $sp^3$ hybridization state with two bonding pairs and two lone pairs. The lone pair-lone pair repulsions squeeze the $\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{H}$ bond angle down to $108.9^\circ$, which is slightly less than the ideal tetrahedral angle of $109^\circ 28'$. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. In methoxymethane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{O}-\text{CH}_3$), the central oxygen atom is also $sp^3$-hybridized. However, the steric hindrance and electrostatic repulsion between the two bulky methyl ($-\text{CH}_3$) groups push the bonds apart, opening the $\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{C}$ angle to $111.7^\circ$, which is slightly greater than $109^\circ 28'$. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both statements are factually accurate NCERT statements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The boiling point of ethanol ($351\text{ K}$) is significantly higher than that of isomeric methoxymethane ($248\text{ K}$).
Reason (R): Ethanol and methoxymethane are functional isomers possessing the same molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}$ and identical molar masses of $46\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion. Ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) possesses a highly polar $\text{O}-\text{H}$ bond, which enables molecules to associate extensively via strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding. In contrast, methoxymethane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{O}-\text{CH}_3$) cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with itself because it lacks an $\text{H}$ atom directly bonded to oxygen; only weaker dipole-dipole interactions exist. Consequently, ethanol has a much higher boiling point ($351\text{ K}$) than methoxymethane ($248\text{ K}$). Thus, the Assertion statement is true.
Step 2: Evaluate the Reason. Both ethanol and methoxymethane share the identical molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}$ and molecular mass ($46\text{ g mol}^{-1}$), making them functional group isomers. Thus, the Reason statement is true.
Step 3: Determine the explanation link. Having the same molecular formula and molar mass does not explain why ethanol has a higher boiling point; the true cause of the boiling point difference is intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding synthetic methods for preparing alcohols:
List I (Reaction):
A. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{(i) } \text{B}_2\text{H}_6, \text{THF}} \xrightarrow{\text{(ii) } \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 / \text{OH}^-}$
B. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}$
C. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}$
D. $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{(i) } \text{LiAlH}_4 / \text{ether}} \xrightarrow{\text{(ii) } \text{H}_2\text{O}}$
List II (Major Product):
I. Propan-1-ol
II. Propan-2-ol
III. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
IV. Ethanol
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
D) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match Reaction A. Hydroboration-oxidation of propene with diborane followed by alkaline hydrogen peroxide yields anti-Markovnikov hydration product, propan-1-ol. Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match Reaction B. Ethanal (an aldehyde other than methanal) reacts with methylmagnesium bromide to yield a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol. Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match Reaction C. Propan-2-one (acetone, a ketone) reacts with methylmagnesium bromide to yield a tertiary alcohol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol (tert-butyl alcohol). Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match Reaction D. Ethanoic acid is reduced by lithium aluminium hydride ($\text{LiAlH}_4$) to ethanol (a primary alcohol). Thus, D matches with IV. This corresponds to the sequence A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following isomeric butyl alcohols of molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$:
(i) Butan-1-ol
(ii) 2-Methylpropan-1-ol
(iii) Butan-2-ol
(iv) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of their boiling points?
options: A) (iv) > (iii) > (ii) > (i)
B) (i) > (iii) > (ii) > (iv)
C) (ii) > (i) > (iii) > (iv)
D) (i) > (ii) > (iii) > (iv)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the effect of branching on boiling points. In isomeric alcohols, as branching increases, the molecule assumes a more compact, spherical shape. This reduces the molecular surface area, leading to weaker van der Waals dispersion forces between molecules and lowering the boiling point.
Step 2: Compare specific NCERT values. Butan-1-ol has an unbranched continuous chain with maximum surface area ($b.p. = 390.3\text{ K}$). 2-Methylpropan-1-ol is a primary alcohol with one methyl branch ($b.p. = 381\text{ K}$). Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol with the hydroxyl group at the interior ($b.p. = 372.5\text{ K}$). 2-Methylpropan-2-ol has the most spherical, highly branched structure ($b.p. = 356\text{ K}$).
Step 3: Establish the order. The decreasing order of boiling points is Butan-1-ol > 2-Methylpropan-1-ol > Butan-2-ol > 2-Methylpropan-2-ol, which corresponds to (i) > (ii) > (iii) > (iv).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the industrial preparation of phenol from cumene:
Statement I: Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidized in the presence of air to form cumene hydroperoxide.
Statement II: Cumene hydroperoxide upon treatment with dilute acid is converted into phenol along with propan-2-one (acetone) as a commercially valuable co-product.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. In the industrial manufacture of phenol, cumene (isopropylbenzene) is treated with atmospheric oxygen (air) at elevated temperatures to produce cumene hydroperoxide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C(CH}_3)_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{H}$). Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Cumene hydroperoxide is subsequently treated with dilute sulphuric acid, undergoing an acid-catalyzed rearrangement (via migration of the phenyl ring to oxygen) to yield phenol and acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$). Acetone is isolated in large quantities as a commercially important by-product, making this method economically favorable. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both statements are accurate NCERT descriptions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An unknown alcohol of molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ reacts with Lucas reagent (a solution of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$) at room temperature and produces turbidity immediately. The unknown alcohol is:
options: A) Butan-1-ol
B) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
C) Butan-2-ol
D) 2-Methylpropan-1-ol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand Lucas reagent and test principle. Lucas reagent consists of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$. It differentiates primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols based on their relative rates of reaction to form insoluble alkyl chlorides, which appear as cloudiness/turbidity.
Step 2: Assess relative reactivity. Tertiary ($3^\circ$) alcohols react immediately at room temperature because tertiary carbocations are highly stable. Secondary ($2^\circ$) alcohols produce turbidity within about 5 minutes. Primary ($1^\circ$) alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature and require heating.
Step 3: Identify the substrate. Among the isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$, 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol ($3^\circ$), so it forms 2-chloro-2-methylpropane immediately, resulting in immediate turbidity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Phenol reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide solution to form sodium phenoxide, whereas ethanol does not react appreciably with aqueous sodium hydroxide.
Reason (R): Phenol is a weaker acid than water, while ethanol is a stronger acid than water.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion. Phenol ($pK_a \approx 10$) is a stronger acid than water ($pK_a = 15.7$) and readily dissolves in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ to form sodium phenoxide and water. In contrast, ethanol ($pK_a \approx 16$) is a weaker acid than water, so its deprotonation by hydroxide ion is unfavorable and the reaction equilibrium lies heavily to the left. Thus, the Assertion statement is true.
Step 2: Evaluate the Reason. Because phenol has a lower $pK_a$ ($10$) than water ($15.7$), phenol is a stronger acid than water. Ethanol has a higher $pK_a$ ($16$) than water, meaning ethanol is a weaker acid than water. Therefore, the statement in the Reason is completely reversed and factually false.
Step 3: Conclusion. The Assertion is true but the Reason is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Passing the vapours of 2-methylpropan-2-ol over heated copper catalyst at $573\text{ K}$ yields which of the following organic compounds as the major product?
options: A) 2-Methylpropanal
B) Butan-2-one
C) Propan-2-one and methanal
D) 2-Methylpropene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Recall the action of heated copper ($\text{Cu}$ at $573\text{ K}$) on alcohols. Primary alcohols undergo catalytic dehydrogenation to yield aldehydes (e.g., ethanol to ethanal). Secondary alcohols undergo catalytic dehydrogenation to yield ketones (e.g., propan-2-ol to propan-2-one).
Step 2: Analyze tertiary alcohols. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol with no $\alpha$-hydrogen atom attached to the carbinol carbon. As a result, dehydrogenation cannot occur.
Step 3: Determine the reaction pathway for tertiary alcohols. Under these vigorous conditions ($573\text{ K}$ over $\text{Cu}$), tertiary alcohols undergo dehydration rather than dehydrogenation to yield alkenes:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Cu}, 573\text{ K}} \text{CH}_2=\text{C(CH}_3)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
The major organic product is 2-methylpropene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding characteristic reactions of phenol:
List I (Reaction):
A. Phenol heated with zinc dust
B. Oxidation of phenol with acidified sodium dichromate ($\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$)
C. Reaction of phenol with neutral aqueous $\text{FeCl}_3$
D. Treating phenol with bromine water ($\text{Br}_2 / \text{H}_2\text{O}$)
List II (Characteristic Product):
I. Benzene
II. $p$-Benzoquinone
III. Violet coloured coordination complex
IV. 2,4,6-Tribromophenol (white precipitate)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
C) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
D) A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match Reaction A. Distillation of phenol with zinc dust reduces the phenolic group to give benzene: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{Zn} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{ZnO}$. Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match Reaction B. Oxidation of phenol with chromic acid or acidified sodium dichromate yields a conjugated diketone, $p$-benzoquinone (benzo-1,4-quinone). Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match Reaction C. Phenol reacts with neutral ferric chloride solution to give a characteristic violet-coloured complex $[\text{Fe(OC}_6\text{H}_5)_6]^{3-}$, used as a diagnostic test. Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match Reaction D. In aqueous solution, phenol ionizes significantly to phenoxide ion, highly activating the ortho and para positions and giving 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate. Thus, D matches with IV. This gives the sequence A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In Williamson ether synthesis, tert-butyl ethyl ether is best prepared by treating sodium tert-butoxide with ethyl bromide. If sodium ethoxide is instead reacted with 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl bromide), the major organic product obtained is:
options: A) Di-tert-butyl ether
B) 2-Methylpropene
C) Diethyl ether
D) 2-Ethoxy-2-methylpropane
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the mechanism of Williamson ether synthesis. The reaction involves nucleophilic attack ($\text{S}_\text{N}2$) of an alkoxide ion on an alkyl halide. For an efficient substitution, the alkyl halide must be primary ($1^\circ$).
Step 2: Analyze the effect of a tertiary alkyl halide. Alkoxide ions are not only nucleophiles but also strong Brønsted bases. When a tertiary alkyl halide such as 2-bromo-2-methylpropane is used, steric hindrance prevents $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ backside attack on the tertiary carbon.
Step 3: Identify the dominant pathway. Instead of substitution, an elimination ($\text{E}2$) reaction predominates completely: sodium ethoxide abstracts a $\beta$-hydrogen from the tert-butyl bromide, yielding 2-methylpropene (isobutylene), ethanol, and sodium bromide. Thus, the major product is 2-methylpropene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the separation of nitrophenols:
Statement I: A mixture of $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol obtained by the nitration of phenol with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$ can be separated by steam distillation.
Statement II: $o$-Nitrophenol is less volatile than $p$-nitrophenol because $o$-nitrophenol forms extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds leading to molecular association.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. The mixture of $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol formed by nitration of phenol with dilute nitric acid at $298\text{ K}$ is separated industrially and in the laboratory by steam distillation. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. $o$-Nitrophenol has adjacent $-\text{OH}$ and $-\text{NO}_2$ groups that form a 6-membered ring through intramolecular hydrogen bonding (chelation). This prevents association with neighboring molecules, lowering its boiling point and making it steam volatile. In contrast, $p$-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds with adjacent molecules, causing association, higher boiling point, and non-volatility in steam. Thus, Statement II is incorrect because $o$-nitrophenol is more volatile, not less volatile, and forms intramolecular, not intermolecular, hydrogen bonds.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Heating 1-methoxypropane with one equivalent of concentrated hydriodic acid ($\text{HI}$) produces which of the following pairs of organic products?
options: A) Methanol and 1-iodopropane
B) Iodomethane and propan-2-ol
C) Methanol and 2-iodopropane
D) Iodomethane and propan-1-ol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the ether structure. 1-Methoxypropane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) contains a methyl group ($1^\circ$) and a propyl group ($1^\circ$).
Step 2: Determine the cleavage mechanism. When an unsymmetrical ether containing primary alkyl groups is cleaved by one equivalent of $\text{HI}$, protonation of the ether oxygen generates an oxonium ion ($\text{CH}_3-\text{O}^+(\text{H})-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$).
Step 3: Evaluate nucleophilic attack. The iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) acts as a nucleophile and attacks via an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism. The attack occurs preferentially at the less sterically hindered alkyl carbon (the methyl carbon rather than the propyl carbon).
Step 4: Identify the products. Cleavage of the $\text{O}-\text{CH}_3$ bond produces iodomethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{I}$) and leaves propan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of acidic strength of the given substituted phenols?
options: A) 4-Nitrophenol > 2-Nitrophenol > 3-Nitrophenol > Phenol > 4-Methylphenol
B) 2-Nitrophenol > 4-Nitrophenol > 3-Nitrophenol > 4-Methylphenol > Phenol
C) 3-Nitrophenol > 4-Nitrophenol > 2-Nitrophenol > Phenol > 4-Methylphenol
D) 4-Nitrophenol > 3-Nitrophenol > 2-Nitrophenol > 4-Methylphenol > Phenol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the effect of substituents on phenol acidity. Electron-withdrawing nitro groups ($-\text{NO}_2$) stabilize the phenoxide ion through $-I$ and $-M$ effects, increasing acidity. Electron-donating methyl groups ($-\text{CH}_3$) destabilize the phenoxide ion via $+I$ and hyperconjugation, decreasing acidity.
Step 2: Compare positions of the nitro group. At the 4-position (para), the $-\text{NO}_2$ group exerts both powerful $-M$ and $-I$ effects without any steric or hydrogen bonding hindrance ($pK_a = 7.15$). At the 2-position (ortho), the $-\text{NO}_2$ group also exerts $-M$ and $-I$, but intramolecular hydrogen bonding in undissociated $o$-nitrophenol stabilizes the molecule and slightly hinders proton release ($pK_a = 7.23$). At the 3-position (meta), resonance delocalization of negative charge is absent; only $-I$ operates ($pK_a = 8.35$).
Step 3: Compare with phenol and 4-methylphenol. Phenol has $pK_a = 10.0$, while 4-methylphenol ($p$-cresol) is less acidic with $pK_a = 10.2$.
Step 4: Establish the order. The correct decreasing order is 4-Nitrophenol > 2-Nitrophenol > 3-Nitrophenol > Phenol > 4-Methylphenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Heating anisole (methoxybenzene) with concentrated hydriodic acid ($\text{HI}$) at $373\text{ K}$ yields phenol and iodomethane as the products.
Reason (R): Anisole is an aromatic ether that undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions predominantly at the ortho and para positions.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion. When anisole is treated with $\text{HI}$, the ether oxygen is protonated. Iodide ion attacks the less hindered methyl carbon via $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ displacement because the aromatic $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond has partial double bond character due to resonance and is resistant to cleavage. Thus, phenol and iodomethane are formed. The Assertion statement is true.
Step 2: Evaluate the Reason. In anisole, the methoxy group ($-\text{OCH}_3$) donates electron density into the ring through resonance ($+M > -I$), increasing electron density primarily at the ortho and para positions and directing incoming electrophiles there. The Reason statement is true.
Step 3: Determine the relationship. The Reason describes the electrophilic substitution behavior of the benzene ring in anisole, which does not explain why nucleophilic cleavage of the alkyl-oxygen bond occurs by $\text{HI}$ to yield phenol and iodomethane. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol is treated with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide to form salicylaldehyde. The reactive electrophilic intermediate that attacks the phenoxide ring is:
options: A) Trichloromethyl carbanion ($:\overline{\text{C}}\text{Cl}_3$)
B) Formyl cation ($\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{HO}$)
C) Dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$)
D) Chloromethyl cation ($\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2\text{Cl}$)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the Reimer-Tiemann reaction. Phenol reacts with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) in the presence of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ at $\approx 340\text{ K}$ to introduce a formyl group ($-\text{CHO}$) ortho to the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group, yielding salicylaldehyde.
Step 2: Generation of the electrophile. Chloroform loses a proton to hydroxide base to generate the trichloromethyl carbanion, which undergoes $\alpha$-elimination of a chloride ion:$$\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons :\overline{\text{C}}\text{Cl}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{-\text{Cl}^-} :\text{CCl}_2$$
Step 3: Identify the electrophile. Dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$) possesses an incomplete octet (six valence electrons) and acts as an electrophile that attacks the nucleophilic phenoxide ring.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Heating ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid produces different products depending on the reaction temperature:
(i) At $413\text{ K}$, compound $\text{X}$ is the major product.
(ii) At $443\text{ K}$, compound $\text{Y}$ is the major product.
Identify compounds $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$, respectively:
options: A) X = Ethene, Y = Ethoxyethane
B) X = Ethyl hydrogen sulphate, Y = Ethene
C) X = Diethyl sulphate, Y = Ethoxyethane
D) X = Ethoxyethane, Y = Ethene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze reaction at $413\text{ K}$. At $413\text{ K}$ ($140^\circ\text{C}$), ethanol in the presence of excess concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ undergoes bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (intermolecular dehydration) where an unprotonated ethanol molecule attacks a protonated ethanol molecule, yielding ethoxyethane (diethyl ether, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OC}_2\text{H}_5$). Thus, $\text{X} = \text{Ethoxyethane}$.
Step 2: Analyze reaction at $443\text{ K}$. At $443\text{ K}$ ($170^\circ\text{C}$), elimination dominates over substitution. Protonated ethanol loses water to form an ethyl carbocation/intermediate, which eliminates a proton to form ethene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$). Thus, $\text{Y} = \text{Ethene}$.
Step 3: Conclusion. $\text{X} = \text{Ethoxyethane}$ and $\text{Y} = \text{Ethene}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding commercially important alcohols and reagents:
List I (Term / Reagent):
A. Methanol
B. Denatured alcohol
C. Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC)
D. Lucas reagent
List II (Description / NCERT Specification):
I. Wood spirit produced by catalytic hydrogenation of carbon monoxide
II. Ethanol made unfit for drinking by adding copper sulphate and pyridine
III. Reagent for selective oxidation of primary alcohols to aldehydes
IV. Equimolar mixture of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
C) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
D) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A. Methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$) was historically known as wood spirit and is manufactured by catalytic hydrogenation of carbon monoxide using $\text{ZnO}-\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3$ catalyst at $573-673\text{ K}$ and $200-300\text{ atm}$. Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match B. Commercial alcohol is made unfit for drinking (denatured) by mixing it with copper sulphate (to impart color) and pyridine (a foul-smelling liquid) or methanol. Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match C. Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC, a complex of chromium trioxide with pyridine and $\text{HCl}$) oxidizes primary alcohols selectively to aldehydes without over-oxidation to carboxylic acids. Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match D. Lucas reagent is an equimolar solution of concentrated hydrochloric acid and anhydrous zinc chloride. Thus, D matches with IV. This matches the sequence A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the reduction of carbonyl compounds to alcohols:
(i) Sodium borohydride ($\text{NaBH}_4$) reduces aldehydes and ketones to primary and secondary alcohols, respectively.
(ii) Sodium borohydride ($\text{NaBH}_4$) readily reduces carboxylic acids and esters to primary alcohols.
(iii) Lithium aluminium hydride ($\text{LiAlH}_4$) reduces carboxylic acids directly to primary alcohols in excellent yield.
(iv) Commercially, carboxylic acids are converted to esters, which are then reduced to alcohols by catalytic hydrogenation.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (i) and (ii) only
B) (i), (iii) and (iv) only
C) (ii), (iii) and (iv) only
D) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze statement (i). $\text{NaBH}_4$ is a mild reducing agent that readily reduces aldehydes to primary alcohols and ketones to secondary alcohols. Statement (i) is correct.
Step 2: Analyze statement (ii). $\text{NaBH}_4$ is not nucleophilic enough to reduce carboxylic acids or esters under standard conditions. Statement (ii) is incorrect.
Step 3: Analyze statement (iii). $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a powerful reducing agent capable of reducing carboxylic acids directly to primary alcohols in high yield. Statement (iii) is correct.
Step 4: Analyze statement (iv). Because $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is an expensive reagent, commercial production of alcohols from acids involves esterification followed by catalytic reduction with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst:$$\text{RCOOH} \xrightarrow{\text{R}'\text{OH}, \text{H}^+} \text{RCOOR}' \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2 / \text{catalyst}} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{R}'\text{OH}$$
Statement (iv) is correct. Thus, statements (i), (iii), and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the cleavage of alkyl aryl ethers by halogen acids:
Statement I: When anisole is heated with concentrated hydriodic acid ($\text{HI}$), the products formed are phenol and iodomethane.
Statement II: Iodobenzene and methanol are formed as major products because the methyl-oxygen bond is stronger than the phenyl-oxygen bond.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. Reaction of anisole with $\text{HI}$ yields protonated anisole ($[\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{O}^+(\text{H})-\text{CH}_3]$). The nucleophilic iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) attacks the methyl group, producing phenol and iodomethane. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. The bond between the $sp^2$-hybridized phenyl carbon and the oxygen atom has partial double bond character due to resonance delocalization of oxygen's lone pair into the aromatic ring. This makes the $\text{C}_\text{aromatic}-\text{O}$ bond much stronger and shorter than the $sp^3$ methyl-oxygen bond. Hence, nucleophilic substitution occurs at the methyl carbon, forming phenol and iodomethane, not iodobenzene and methanol. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In Kolbe's reaction, the primary major product formed upon treating sodium phenoxide with carbon dioxide at $400\text{ K}$ and $4-7\text{ atm}$ followed by acidification is 4-hydroxybenzoic acid.
Reason (R): In alkaline medium, the phenoxide ion is substantially more reactive than phenol towards electrophilic aromatic substitution and undergoes attack by the weak electrophile carbon dioxide.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion. In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide is heated with carbon dioxide at $400\text{ K}$ and $4-7\text{ atm}$ pressure, followed by acidification to produce 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid) as the predominant major product, not 4-hydroxybenzoic acid. Thus, the Assertion statement is false.
Step 2: Evaluate the Reason. Phenoxide ion carries a full negative charge, which is delocalized into the benzene ring, making it significantly more nucleophilic and activating the ring far more than neutral phenol. This enhanced reactivity allows it to undergo electrophilic substitution with carbon dioxide, which is a weak electrophile. Thus, the Reason statement is true.
Step 3: Conclusion. The Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the acidity and chemical reactions of alcohols:
Statement I: Alcohols react with active metals such as sodium, potassium, and aluminium to form the corresponding alkoxides and liberate dihydrogen gas.
Statement II: In their reactions with active metals, alcohols act as Brønsted acids by donating a proton to form hydrogen gas.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. Alcohols react with strongly electropositive metals such as $\text{Na}$, $\text{K}$, and $\text{Al}$ to yield metal alkoxides and dihydrogen gas:
$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \to 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$6(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH} + 2\text{Al} \to 2[(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-O}]_3\text{Al} + 3\text{H}_2$$
Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. A Brønsted acid is defined as a proton donor. In the reaction with active metals, the alcohol molecule donates its hydroxyl proton (which accepts an electron from the metal to form hydrogen atom and recombines to form $\text{H}_2$). Thus, alcohols demonstrate acidic character according to the Brønsted-Lowry definition. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When phenol is treated with bromine dissolved in carbon disulphide ($\text{CS}_2$) at $273\text{ K}$, compound $\text{P}$ is obtained as the major product. When phenol is treated with bromine water at room temperature, compound $\text{Q}$ is obtained as a white precipitate. Identify $\text{P}$ and $\text{Q}$, respectively:
options: A) P = 2-Bromophenol, Q = 4-Bromophenol
B) P = 4-Bromophenol, Q = 2,4,6-Tribromophenol
C) P = 2,4,6-Tribromophenol, Q = 4-Bromophenol
D) P = 3-Bromophenol, Q = 2,4-Dibromophenol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze reaction in non-polar solvent. In solvents of low polarity such as carbon disulphide ($\text{CS}_2$) or chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) at low temperature ($273\text{ K}$), the ionization of phenol to phenoxide ion is negligible. Phenol itself undergoes monobromination to give 4-bromophenol ($p$-bromophenol) as the major product due to less steric hindrance, along with minor 2-bromophenol. Thus, $\text{P} = \text{4-Bromophenol}$.
Step 2: Analyze reaction in aqueous medium. In water, phenol ionizes extensively to phenoxide ion. The phenoxide ion strongly activates the ortho and para positions of the aromatic ring through $+M$ electron donation. Consequently, all three activated positions are brominated simultaneously, yielding 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate. Thus, $\text{Q} = \text{2,4,6-Tribromophenol}$.
Step 3: Conclusion. $\text{P} = \text{4-Bromophenol}$ and $\text{Q} = \text{2,4,6-Tribromophenol}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When 3-methylbut-1-ene is subjected to acid-catalysed hydration using dilute sulphuric acid, the major organic product obtained is:
options: A) 3-Methylbutan-1-ol
B) 3-Methylbutan-2-ol
C) 2-Methylbutan-2-ol
D) 2-Methylbut-2-ene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Protonation of alkene. Electrophilic addition of a proton ($\text{H}^+$) to the double bond of 3-methylbut-1-ene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$) occurs in accordance with Markovnikov's rule to produce a secondary carbocation:$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_3$$
Step 2: Carbocation rearrangement. The adjacent tertiary carbon holds a hydrogen atom. A 1,2-hydride shift occurs rapidly from the tertiary carbon to the secondary carbocation carbon to form a substantially more stable tertiary carbocation:$$\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$$
Step 3: Nucleophilic attack and deprotonation. Water attacks the tertiary carbocation to form an oxonium ion, followed by loss of a proton to yield 2-methylbutan-2-ol as the major product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the cleavage of unsymmetrical ethers by hydriodic acid:
Statement I: In the cleavage of $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{CH}_3$ with cold $\text{HI}$, the reaction proceeds via an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism to yield $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$.
Statement II: In the reaction of tert-butyl methyl ether with $\text{HI}$, an exceptionally stable tertiary carbocation is generated, directing the reaction pathway through an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism to give $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-I}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. When one of the alkyl groups attached to the ether oxygen is tertiary, cleavage does not follow an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ pathway. Because steric hindrance prevents backside attack on the tertiary carbon and a stable tertiary carbocation can form, the reaction proceeds via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway yielding $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-I}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Upon protonation of tert-butyl methyl ether, the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond between the tert-butyl group and oxygen cleaves to yield a stable tert-butyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$) and neutral methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$). Subsequent rapid attack of iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) on the tert-butyl carbocation yields 2-iodo-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl iodide). Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The rate of acid-catalysed esterification of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid decreases sharply in the order: $\text{CH}_3\text{OH} > \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHOH} > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$.
Reason (R): Esterification involves nucleophilic attack of the alcohol oxygen on the protonated carbonyl carbon, and increased steric crowding around the hydroxyl group in bulky alcohols hinders nucleophilic approach to the tetrahedral intermediate.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion. Acid-catalysed Fischer esterification is highly sensitive to steric hindrance in both the carboxylic acid and the alcohol. The reactivity of alcohols decreases in the order: methyl alcohol > primary alcohol > secondary alcohol > tertiary alcohol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH} > 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$). Thus, the Assertion statement is true.
Step 2: Evaluate the Reason. During esterification, the alcohol acts as a nucleophile, attacking the protonated carbonyl carbon to form a crowded tetrahedral intermediate. Bulky alkyl substituents on the alcohol increase steric crowding in the transition state leading to this intermediate, substantially increasing the activation energy and diminishing the reaction rate. Thus, the Reason statement is true.
Step 3: Determine the explanation link. The steric hindrance identified in the Reason is the direct causal explanation for the observed reactivity sequence described in the Assertion. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions of anisole (methoxybenzene):
(i) Bromination of anisole with bromine in ethanoic acid yields 4-bromoanisole in about $90\%$ yield even in the absence of an iron(III) bromide catalyst.
(ii) Friedel-Crafts alkylation of anisole with chloromethane in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride yields 4-methoxytoluene as the major product.
(iii) In electrophilic substitution reactions, the methoxy group ($-\text{OCH}_3$) acts as a meta-directing group because oxygen is more electronegative than carbon.
(iv) Nitration of anisole with a mixture of concentrated sulphuric and nitric acids yields a mixture of 2-nitroanisole and 4-nitroanisole, with 4-nitroanisole as the major product.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (i) and (iii) only
B) (i), (ii) and (iv) only
C) (ii), (iii) and (iv) only
D) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze statement (i). The methoxy group ($-\text{OCH}_3$) strongly activates the benzene ring via $+M$ resonance, so halogenation occurs smoothly without requiring a Lewis acid catalyst like $\text{FeBr}_3$. Bromination with $\text{Br}_2$ in ethanoic acid yields $90\%$ 4-bromoanisole (para-isomer). Statement (i) is correct.
Step 2: Analyze statement (ii). Anisole reacts with $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to yield 4-methoxytoluene as the major product and 2-methoxytoluene as the minor product. Statement (ii) is correct.
Step 3: Analyze statement (iii). The unshared electron pair on oxygen is delocalized into the $\pi$-electron system of the ring through resonance ($+M$), which increases electron density at the ortho and para positions. Therefore, the methoxy group is ortho/para-directing, not meta-directing. Statement (iii) is incorrect.
Step 4: Analyze statement (iv). Nitration of anisole with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ produces a mixture of ortho and para nitroanisoles, with 4-nitroanisole being the major product due to minimal steric hindrance. Statement (iv) is correct. Thus, statements (i), (ii), and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the dehydration of alcohols to alkenes:
List I (Alcohol):
A. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (Butan-1-ol)
B. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH}$ (2-Methylpropan-2-ol)
C. $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH(OH)CH}_3$ (3-Methylbutan-2-ol)
D. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (Ethanol at $443\text{ K}$)
List II (Major Alkene Formed upon Dehydration):
I. But-2-ene
II. 2-Methylpropene
III. 2-Methylbut-2-ene
IV. Ethene
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
D) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match Alcohol A. Dehydration of butan-1-ol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ involves loss of water to form a primary carbocation, which rearranges via a 1,2-hydride shift to a more stable secondary carbocation. Elimination of a proton then yields the more substituted and thermodynamically stable but-2-ene according to Saytzeff's rule. Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match Alcohol B. Dehydration of 2-methylpropan-2-ol forms a stable tertiary carbocation which eliminates a proton directly to give 2-methylpropene. Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match Alcohol C. Dehydration of 3-methylbutan-2-ol produces a secondary carbocation that undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to form a tertiary carbocation, yielding the highly substituted alkene 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product. Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match Alcohol D. Dehydration of ethanol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $443\text{ K}$ yields ethene. Thus, D matches with IV. This corresponds to the sequence A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) is converted into acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin, a widely used analgesic and antipyretic) by reaction with:
options: A) Methanol in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
B) Acetone in the presence of dry $\text{HCl}$ gas
C) Benzoyl chloride in the presence of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$
D) Acetic anhydride in the presence of a few drops of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the structure of aspirin. Aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid (2-acetoxybenzoic acid), in which the phenolic hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) group of salicylic acid is converted into an acetate ester ($-\text{OCOCH}_3$).
Step 2: Identify the acetylation reagent. Acetylation of the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group is carried out by heating salicylic acid with acetic anhydride ($(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}$) in the presence of a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid (or phosphoric acid) as a catalyst:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{OH})(\text{COOH}) + (\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{OCOCH}_3)(\text{COOH}) + \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
Step 3: Evaluate other options. Methanol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ reacts with the carboxyl group to form methyl salicylate (oil of wintergreen). Thus, acetylation to aspirin requires acetic anhydride in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the synthesis of picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol):
Statement I: Direct nitration of phenol with concentrated nitric acid produces picric acid in very poor yield because a substantial portion of the phenol is oxidized by the strong oxidizing nature of concentrated nitric acid.
Statement II: Industrially, picric acid is prepared by first treating phenol with concentrated sulphuric acid to form phenol-2,4-disulphonic acid, which is subsequently heated with concentrated nitric acid.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. Direct treatment of phenol with concentrated nitric acid leads to extensive oxidative degradation and charring because phenol is an activated aromatic ring and concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ is a powerful oxidizing agent. Consequently, the yield of 2,4,6-trinitrophenol is extremely poor. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. To prevent destructive oxidation, phenol is first sulphonated with concentrated sulphuric acid to produce phenol-2,4-disulphonic acid. The introduced sulphonic acid groups ($-\text{SO}_3\text{H}$) deactivate the ring against oxidation. Subsequent treatment with concentrated nitric acid replaces the sulphonic acid groups via ipso-substitution along with nitration at the remaining position, yielding picric acid in high yield. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Hydroboration-oxidation of propene yields propan-1-ol as the major product.
Reason (R): Hydroboration involves the addition of a borane molecule across the carbon-carbon double bond via a cyclic four-membered transition state.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion. Treatment of propene with diborane followed by oxidation with alkaline hydrogen peroxide results in net anti-Markovnikov addition of water across the double bond, yielding propan-1-ol as the major product. Thus, the Assertion statement is true.
Step 2: Evaluate the Reason. In the addition of borane ($\text{BH}_3$) to the alkene double bond, the boron atom and a hydrogen atom add concertedly across the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond through a cyclic four-membered transition state. Thus, the Reason statement is true.
Step 3: Determine the explanation link. The anti-Markovnikov regioselectivity of the addition is governed specifically by steric hindrance (the boron atom prefers the less substituted, less crowded terminal carbon) and electronic stabilization in the transition state. Simply stating that the addition proceeds via a four-membered transition state does not explain why the boron atom attaches to the terminal carbon rather than the internal carbon. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding named organic transformations of phenol:
List I (Reaction):
A. Sodium phenoxide $+ \text{CO}_2 \xrightarrow{400\text{ K}, 4-7\text{ atm}} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+}$
B. Phenol $+ \text{CHCl}_3 + \text{aq. NaOH} \xrightarrow{340\text{ K}} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+}$
C. Phenol $+ \text{dilute } \text{HNO}_3 \xrightarrow{298\text{ K}}$
D. Phenol $+ (\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{pyridine}}$
List II (Major Product / Mixture):
I. Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid)
II. Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde)
III. Mixture of 2-nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol
IV. Phenyl ethanoate (phenyl acetate)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
D) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match Reaction A. In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide is heated with carbon dioxide at $400\text{ K}$ and $4-7\text{ atm}$ pressure, followed by acidification to produce salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match Reaction B. In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol is heated with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide at $340\text{ K}$, followed by acidification to yield salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde). Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match Reaction C. Nitration of phenol with dilute nitric acid at room temperature ($298\text{ K}$) yields a mixture of 2-nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol. Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match Reaction D. Acetylation of phenol with acetic anhydride in the presence of pyridine yields phenyl ethanoate (an ester). Thus, D matches with IV. This gives the sequence A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following five phenolic compounds and their acid dissociation constants ($pK_a$):
(I) 4-Nitrophenol
(II) 2-Nitrophenol
(III) 3-Nitrophenol
(IV) Phenol
(V) 4-Methylphenol
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding these compounds?
options: A) 4-Nitrophenol is a stronger acid than 2-nitrophenol because intramolecular hydrogen bonding in 2-nitrophenol stabilizes the undissociated molecule
B) 3-Nitrophenol is more acidic than phenol because the nitro group exerts an electron-withdrawing $-I$ inductive effect
C) 4-Methylphenol is less acidic than phenol because the methyl group destabilizes the phenoxide anion via $+I$ and hyperconjugative electron release
D) The $pK_a$ value of 4-nitrophenol is higher than the $pK_a$ value of phenol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the relation between acidity and $pK_a$. Acidic strength is inversely proportional to $pK_a$ value ($pK_a = -\log_{10} K_a$). A stronger acid has a larger $K_a$ value and therefore a smaller (lower) $pK_a$ value.
Step 2: Check values from NCERT. 4-Nitrophenol has a $pK_a$ of $7.15$, 2-nitrophenol has $7.23$, 3-nitrophenol has $8.35$, phenol has $10.0$, and 4-methylphenol has $10.2$.
Step 3: Evaluate statement D. Since 4-nitrophenol ($pK_a = 7.15$) is substantially more acidic than phenol ($pK_a = 10.0$), the $pK_a$ of 4-nitrophenol is lower than that of phenol, not higher. Thus, the statement stating that the $pK_a$ of 4-nitrophenol is higher than that of phenol is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements regarding the oxidation of alcohols is correct?
options: A) Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) selectively oxidizes primary allylic and benzylic alcohols to corresponding unsaturated or aromatic aldehydes without cleaving carbon-carbon double bonds
B) Alkaline potassium permanganate oxidizes secondary alcohols cleanly into aldehydes
C) Anhydrous chromium trioxide ($\text{CrO}_3$) in glacial acetic acid oxidizes tertiary alcohols directly to carboxylic acids without loss of carbon atoms
D) Dehydrogenation of a primary alcohol over heated copper catalyst at $573\text{ K}$ yields a symmetrical ketone
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze oxidation with pyridinium chlorochromate. Pyridinium chlorochromate ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_5\text{NH}^+\text{CrO}_3\text{Cl}^-$, PCC) in anhydrous dichloromethane ($\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$) is a mild and selective oxidizing agent. It oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without oxidizing the product further to carboxylic acid and without attacking isolated carbon-carbon double bonds. This statement is chemically correct.
Step 2: Analyze potassium permanganate oxidation. Secondary alcohols are oxidized by strong oxidizing agents like $\text{KMnO}_4$ or $\text{CrO}_3$ to ketones, not aldehydes. Thus, the statement regarding potassium permanganate is incorrect.
Step 3: Analyze chromium trioxide. Tertiary alcohols have no $\alpha$-hydrogen and are resistant to oxidation; under vigorous conditions with strong oxidants, they undergo carbon-carbon cleavage to yield carboxylic acids containing fewer carbon atoms than the starting alcohol. Thus, the statement regarding chromium trioxide is incorrect.
Step 4: Analyze copper dehydrogenation. Catalytic dehydrogenation of primary alcohols over $\text{Cu}$ at $573\text{ K}$ yields aldehydes, not ketones. Thus, the statement regarding copper dehydrogenation is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Dialkyl ethers possess a non-zero dipole moment even when the two alkyl groups attached to the oxygen atom are identical (e.g., diethyl ether has $\mu \approx 1.18\text{ D}$).
Reason (R): Ethers are prepared on an industrial scale by the acid-catalysed intermolecular dehydration of primary alcohols at $413\text{ K}$.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion. In ethers, the oxygen atom is $sp^3$-hybridized and possesses two bonding pairs and two lone pairs of electrons. The $\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{C}$ bond angle is approximately $111.7^\circ$, giving the molecule an angular (bent) geometry. Because the two polar $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond dipole vectors point in opposite directions at an angle and do not lie in a straight line, they do not cancel each other out, resulting in a net dipole moment ($\mu \approx 1.18\text{ D}$ for diethyl ether). Thus, the Assertion statement is true.
Step 2: Evaluate the Reason. Industrially, diethyl ether is prepared by heating excess ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid at $413\text{ K}$ ($140^\circ\text{C}$). Thus, the Reason statement is true.
Step 3: Determine the explanation link. The synthetic industrial preparation of ethers by alcohol dehydration has no causal connection to the geometric arrangement of bonds or the dipole moment of ethers. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following ether cleavage reactions carried out with hydriodic acid ($\text{HI}$):
(i) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + 2\text{HI (excess)} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{I} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
(ii) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{O}-\text{CH}_3 + \text{HI (excess)} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{I} + \text{CH}_3\text{I} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
(iii) $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{CH}_3 + \text{HI (cold)} \to (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-I} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$
(iv) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HI (cold)} \to \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{I} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
Which of the above equations correctly depict the organic products formed?
options: A) (i) and (ii) only
B) (ii) and (iii) only
C) (i), (iii) and (iv) only
D) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate equation (i). Diethyl ether heated with excess concentrated $\text{HI}$ first gives ethyl iodide and ethanol; the ethanol then reacts with the second mole of $\text{HI}$ to give a second mole of ethyl iodide. Equation (i) is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate equation (ii). In anisole, the $\text{C}_\text{aromatic}-\text{O}$ bond possesses partial double bond character due to resonance and cannot be cleaved under these conditions. Even with excess $\text{HI}$, the products are phenol and iodomethane; iodobenzene is never formed. Equation (ii) is incorrect.
Step 3: Evaluate equation (iii). In tert-butyl methyl ether, cleavage proceeds via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway through the stable tert-butyl carbocation to yield tert-butyl iodide and methanol. Equation (iii) is correct.
Step 4: Evaluate equation (iv). In benzyl ethyl ether, the benzyl-oxygen bond readily dissociates via a very stable benzylic intermediate/carbocation (or facile benzylic displacement), yielding benzyl iodide and ethanol. Equation (iv) is correct. Thus, equations (i), (iii), and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
The mechanism of acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol to ethene involves three distinct sequential steps:
Step 1: Protonation of ethanol to form ethyl oxonium ion.
Step 2: Dissociation of ethyl oxonium ion to form an ethyl carbocation.
Step 3: Elimination of a proton to generate ethene.
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding this mechanism?
options: A) Step 1 is a rapid, reversible Brønsted acid-base equilibrium
B) Step 2 is the slowest, rate-determining step of the reaction
C) The ease of dehydration of alcohols follows the order $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$ because it is governed by carbocation stability
D) The sulphuric acid catalyst is consumed irreversibly during Step 1 and is not regenerated in the reaction
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Step 1. In Step 1, ethanol acts as a Lewis/Brønsted base and rapidly accepts a proton from sulphuric acid to form the protonated alcohol (ethyl oxonium ion). This is a fast, reversible equilibrium.
Step 2: Analyze Step 2. Cleavage of the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond to release a water molecule and generate the carbocation is the slowest step requiring maximum activation energy, making it the rate-determining step.
Step 3: Analyze dehydration ease. Because carbocation formation is rate-determining, more stable carbocations form faster. Tertiary carbocations are most stable, so dehydration ease is $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$.
Step 4: Analyze catalyst regeneration. In Step 3, the carbocation loses a proton from the $\beta$-carbon to a base (such as $\text{HSO}_4^-$ or water), which regenerates the acid catalyst ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$). Thus, the catalyst is regenerated, not consumed irreversibly. Therefore, the statement asserting that the sulphuric acid catalyst is consumed irreversibly is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the synthesis of phenol from haloarenes:
Statement I: Conversion of chlorobenzene to phenol (Dow's process) requires drastic reaction conditions ($623\text{ K}$ and $300\text{ atm}$ pressure) with aqueous sodium hydroxide followed by acidification.
Statement II: The presence of strong electron-withdrawing nitro groups ($-\text{NO}_2$) at positions ortho and para to chlorine significantly increases the rate of nucleophilic aromatic substitution, allowing the reaction to proceed under substantially milder conditions.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. Chlorobenzene is extremely unreactive towards nucleophilic substitution due to resonance stabilization (partial double bond character of the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond), $sp^2$ hybridization of the ring carbon, and repulsion between the incoming nucleophile and the $\pi$-electron cloud. Hence, conversion to sodium phenoxide requires severe conditions: aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ at $623\text{ K}$ and $300\text{ atm}$ pressure, followed by acidification. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. When electron-withdrawing groups like $-\text{NO}_2$ are present at ortho and para positions, they stabilize the anionic Meisenheimer intermediate by withdrawing negative charge into the nitro group via resonance ($-M$). Consequently, 4-chloronitrobenzene reacts at $443\text{ K}$, 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene reacts with warm aqueous $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ at $368\text{ K}$, and 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene undergoes substitution simply on warming with water. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclusion. Both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following pairs of reactants will successfully yield the tertiary alcohol 2-methylbutan-2-ol upon reaction in dry ether followed by acidic hydrolysis?
options: A) Propanal and ethylmagnesium bromide
B) Butan-2-one and methylmagnesium bromide
C) Butanal and methylmagnesium bromide
D) Methanal and sec-butylmagnesium bromide
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze target molecule. The target alcohol is 2-methylbutan-2-ol:$$\text{CH}_3-\text{C(OH)(CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
This is a tertiary alcohol containing three alkyl groups attached to the carbinol carbon: two methyl groups and one ethyl group.
Step 2: Evaluate reaction of propanal with ethylmagnesium bromide. Propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$) reacting with ethylmagnesium bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{MgBr}$) yields pentan-3-ol, which is a secondary alcohol ($2^\circ$).
Step 3: Evaluate reaction of butan-2-one with methylmagnesium bromide. Butan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) reacts with methylmagnesium bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$) by nucleophilic addition of the methyl group to the carbonyl carbon, producing the magnesium alkoxide intermediate $[\text{CH}_3-\text{C(OMgBr)(CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3]$. Subsequent acidic hydrolysis yields 2-methylbutan-2-ol ($3^\circ$). Thus, this reaction pair successfully produces the desired alcohol.
Step 4: Evaluate remaining combinations. Butanal with methylmagnesium bromide gives pentan-2-ol ($2^\circ$). Methanal with sec-butylmagnesium bromide gives 2-methylbutan-1-ol ($1^\circ$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Diethyl ether shows considerable solubility in water ($7.5\text{ g}$ per $100\text{ mL}$ of water), which is of the same order of magnitude as that of butan-1-ol ($9\text{ g}$ per $100\text{ mL}$).
Reason (R): Ethers are capable of forming strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other in the pure liquid state just like alcohols.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion. Diethyl ether and butan-1-ol have similar molar masses ($74\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) and show comparable solubility in water ($7.5\text{ g}$ per $100\text{ mL}$ for diethyl ether versus $9.0\text{ g}$ per $100\text{ mL}$ for butan-1-ol). This is because the unshared electron pairs on the ether oxygen can accept hydrogen bonds from water molecules ($\text{R}_2\text{O}\cdots\text{H}-\text{O}-\text{H}$). Thus, the Assertion statement is true.
Step 2: Evaluate the Reason. Ethers do not have a hydrogen atom directly bonded to an electronegative oxygen atom. Consequently, ether molecules cannot form hydrogen bonds with one another in the pure state; only weak dipole-dipole interactions exist. Thus, the Reason statement is false.
Step 3: Conclusion. The Assertion is true but the Reason is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding temperature-controlled electrophilic substitutions of phenol:
List I (Reaction Conditions):
A. Phenol $+ \text{conc. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \text{ at } 293\text{ K}$
B. Phenol $+ \text{conc. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \text{ at } 373\text{ K}$
C. Phenol $+ \text{dilute } \text{HNO}_3 \text{ at } 298\text{ K}$
D. Phenol $+ \text{conc. } \text{HNO}_3$ (direct nitration)
List II (Predominant Product / Reaction Outcome):
I. 2-Hydroxybenzenesulphonic acid ($o$-product, kinetically controlled)
II. 4-Hydroxybenzenesulphonic acid ($p$-product, thermodynamically controlled)
III. Mixture of $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol
IV. 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol in poor yield due to destructive oxidation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
D) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match A. Sulphonation of phenol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at low temperature ($293\text{ K}$) is kinetically controlled, yielding 2-hydroxybenzenesulphonic acid ($o$-isomer) as the major product. Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match B. At higher temperature ($373\text{ K}$), sulphonation is reversible and thermodynamically controlled, yielding 4-hydroxybenzenesulphonic acid ($p$-isomer) as the major product because it has less steric hindrance. Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match C. Nitration of phenol with dilute nitric acid at room temperature ($298\text{ K}$) yields a mixture of $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol. Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match D. Direct treatment of phenol with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ causes significant oxidation and charring of the ring, giving 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) in poor yield. Thus, D matches with IV. This matches the sequence A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following qualitative diagnostic chemical tests for distinguishing alcohols and phenols:
(i) Phenol gives a characteristic violet coloration upon reaction with neutral aqueous ferric chloride solution, whereas ethanol gives no coloration.
(ii) Ethanol gives a yellow precipitate of triiodomethane (iodoform) upon warming with iodine and aqueous sodium hydroxide, whereas methanol gives a negative test.
(iii) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol produces cloudiness immediately with Lucas reagent at room temperature, whereas butan-1-ol produces no cloudiness at room temperature.
(iv) Phenol produces brisk effervescence of carbon dioxide gas upon treatment with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate solution.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (i), (ii) and (iii) only
B) (i) and (iv) only
C) (ii), (iii) and (iv) only
D) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze statement (i). Neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ reacts with phenol to form a violet coordination complex $[\text{Fe(OC}_6\text{H}_5)_6]^{3-}$, while aliphatic alcohols do not give this coloration. Statement (i) is correct.
Step 2: Analyze statement (ii). The iodoform test is given by compounds containing the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group. Ethanol has the structure $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, so it oxidizes to ethanal and yields a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$). Methanol lacks this unit and does not give the test. Statement (ii) is correct.
Step 3: Analyze statement (iii). 2-Methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol that forms an insoluble alkyl chloride immediately with Lucas reagent at room temperature. Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol that does not react at room temperature. Statement (iii) is correct.
Step 4: Analyze statement (iv). Phenol ($pK_a \approx 10$) is a weaker acid than carbonic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$, $pK_a \approx 6.4$), so it cannot liberate $\text{CO}_2$ from sodium bicarbonate ($\text{NaHCO}_3$). Statement (iv) is incorrect. Thus, statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When 1-cyclopentylethanol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid, it undergoes carbocation rearrangement involving ring expansion. The major alkene product obtained from this reaction is:
options: A) Ethylidenecyclopentane
B) 1-Methylcyclohexene
C) 3-Methylcyclohexene
D) Cyclopentyleethene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Protonation and water departure. Protonation of 1-cyclopentylethanol ($c\text{-C}_5\text{H}_9-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3$) followed by loss of a water molecule produces a secondary carbocation on the side chain ($c\text{-C}_5\text{H}_9-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_3$).
Step 2: Ring expansion. The secondary carbocation is adjacent to a strained five-membered cyclopentyl ring. Migration of an endocyclic $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond from the five-membered ring to the positively charged carbon expands the ring to a six-membered cyclohexane ring, relieving ring strain and producing a secondary cyclohexyl carbocation (2-methylcyclohexyl cation).
Step 3: Hydride shift and Saytzeff elimination. A subsequent 1,2-hydride shift converts the secondary cyclohexyl carbocation into a more stable tertiary 1-methylcyclohexyl carbocation. Loss of a proton from the adjacent methylene carbon yields the tetrasubstituted, thermodynamically most stable alkene, 1-methylcyclohexene, as the major Saytzeff product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding hydration methods for alkenes:
Statement I: Hydroboration-oxidation of an unsymmetrical alkene involves concerted syn-addition of $\text{H}$ and $\text{B}$ across the double bond without carbocation rearrangement, yielding an anti-Markovnikov alcohol with retention of configuration at the carbon bonded to boron.
Statement II: Oxymercuration-demercuration of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene proceeds via an open classical carbocation intermediate that undergoes a rapid 1,2-methyl shift to yield 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol as the major product.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. In hydroboration-oxidation, diborane adds to the alkene via a concerted four-membered cyclic transition state where $\text{H}$ and $\text{B}$ add to the same face (syn-addition). No discrete carbocation is generated, so rearrangements do not occur. Oxidation of the trialkylborane by alkaline $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ replaces the $\text{C}-\text{B}$ bond with a $\text{C}-\text{OH}$ bond with complete retention of stereochemical configuration, resulting in net anti-Markovnikov hydration. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Oxymercuration-demercuration involves the formation of a bridged cyclic mercurinium ion intermediate rather than an open classical carbocation. Because the cyclic intermediate prevents carbocation rearrangement, hydration occurs strictly with Markovnikov regioselectivity without skeletal rearrangement. For 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene, oxymercuration-demercuration yields 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol, not the rearranged product 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.
Step 3: Conclusion. Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction of phenol with chloroform in aqueous sodium hydroxide, the primary electrophilic intermediate attacking the aromatic ring is the trichloromethyl carbanion ($:\overline{\text{C}}\text{Cl}_3$).
Reason (R): Dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$) is an electron-deficient neutral species containing a sextet of valence electrons that acts as an electrophile towards the electron-rich phenoxide ring.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion. In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) reacts with hydroxide ion to generate the trichloromethyl carbanion ($:\overline{\text{C}}\text{Cl}_3$). However, the carbanion is not the electrophile; it spontaneously loses a chloride ion ($\alpha$-elimination) to produce dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$). It is dichlorocarbene that attacks the phenoxide ring as the electrophile. Thus, the Assertion statement is false.
Step 2: Evaluate the Reason. Dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$) possesses only six valence electrons around the carbon atom (an incomplete octet) and an empty $p$-orbital, making it a neutral, strongly electron-deficient electrophile. It readily undergoes electrophilic addition to the nucleophilic phenoxide ring at the ortho position. Thus, the Reason statement is true.
Step 3: Conclusion. The Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following multi-step reaction sequence:
$$\text{Benzene} \xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2, \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4} \text{Compound A} \xrightarrow{\text{O}_2, 403-408\text{ K}} \text{Compound B} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{Compound C} + \text{Compound D}$$
When Compound $\text{C}$ is heated with chloroform and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ followed by acidification, Compound $\text{E}$ is obtained. When Compound $\text{D}$ is warmed with iodine and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, a yellow precipitate is formed.
Identify Compounds $\text{C}$, $\text{D}$, and $\text{E}$, respectively:
options: A) C = Phenol, D = Propan-2-one, E = Salicylaldehyde
B) C = Propan-2-one, D = Phenol, E = Salicylic acid
C) C = Phenol, D = Propan-1-ol, E = Benzoic acid
D) C = Salicylaldehyde, D = Propan-2-one, E = Phenol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify Compounds A and B. Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with propene in the presence of phosphoric acid yields isopropylbenzene (cumene, Compound A). Aerobic oxidation of cumene at $403-408\text{ K}$ yields cumene hydroperoxide (Compound B).
Step 2: Identify Compounds C and D. Acid-catalysed rearrangement of cumene hydroperoxide with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ cleaves the molecule into phenol (Compound C) and propan-2-one (acetone, Compound D). Acetone contains a methyl ketone ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$) group and forms a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$) with $\text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH}$.
Step 3: Identify Compound E. Phenol (Compound C) treated with chloroform and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ undergoes the Reimer-Tiemann reaction to form salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde, Compound E). Thus, $\text{C} = \text{Phenol}$, $\text{D} = \text{Propan-2-one}$, and $\text{E} = \text{Salicylaldehyde}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding selective oxidations and reductions of oxygen-containing functional groups:
List I (Chemical Transformation):
A. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \to \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$
B. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \to \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$
C. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 \to \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$
D. $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \to \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
List II (Most Suitable Reagent):
I. Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$
II. Alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification
III. $\text{NaBH}_4$ in ethanol
IV. $\text{LiAlH}_4$ in dry ether followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
B) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
C) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
D) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match Transformation A. Oxidation of an allylic primary alcohol (but-2-en-1-ol) to an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated aldehyde (but-2-enal) without oxidizing the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond requires the mild, selective oxidant pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC). Thus, A matches with I.
Step 2: Match Transformation B. Direct conversion of a primary alcohol (propan-1-ol) to a carboxylic acid (propanoic acid) requires a strong oxidizing agent like alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ or acidified potassium dichromate. Thus, B matches with II.
Step 3: Match Transformation C. Clean reduction of a ketone (acetone) to a secondary alcohol (propan-2-ol) is carried out efficiently and safely using $\text{NaBH}_4$ in ethanol. Thus, C matches with III.
Step 4: Match Transformation D. Reduction of an ester (ethyl ethanoate) to primary alcohols (ethanol) requires a powerful hydride donor like $\text{LiAlH}_4$ because $\text{NaBH}_4$ does not reduce esters under normal conditions. Thus, D matches with IV. This matches the sequence A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the cleavage of the following two unsymmetrical ethers with one equivalent of concentrated hydriodic acid ($\text{HI}$) at room temperature:
Ether 1: Benzyl methyl ether ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_3$)
Ether 2: tert-Butyl ethyl ether ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$)
Which of the following correctly identifies the major alkyl iodide formed from Ether 1 and Ether 2, respectively?
options: A) Methyl iodide and Ethyl iodide
B) Methyl iodide and tert-Butyl iodide
C) Benzyl iodide and tert-Butyl iodide
D) Benzyl iodide and Ethyl iodide
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze cleavage of Ether 1 (benzyl methyl ether). Upon protonation of the ether oxygen to form $[\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2-\text{O}^+(\text{H})-\text{CH}_3]$, the benzylic $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond is remarkably weak due to resonance stabilization of the developing benzylic carbocation. Nucleophilic attack by iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) occurs predominantly at the benzylic carbon (via $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ or fast benzylic $\text{S}_\text{N}2$), yielding benzyl iodide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{I}$) and methanol.
Step 2: Analyze cleavage of Ether 2 (tert-butyl ethyl ether). Protonation gives $[(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{O}^+(\text{H})-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3]$. Because the tert-butyl group generates an exceptionally stable $3^\circ$ carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$) upon heterolysis, the reaction proceeds through an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism. The tertiary carbocation captures iodide ion to form 2-iodo-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl iodide), leaving ethanol.
